sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Colum Eastwood (born 30 April 1983) is an Irish nationalist politician who served as Leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP) from 2015 to 2024.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He has served as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Foyle since 2019, served in the Northern Ireland Assembly from 2011 to 2019 and served on Derry City Council from 2005 to 2011.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Eastwood was first elected to the Northern Ireland Assembly in 2011 and was re-elected in 2016 and 2017.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He was also the SDLP candidate at the 2019 European Parliament election to represent Northern Ireland.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: In December 2019 he was elected to the British House of Commons as the Member of Parliament (MP) for Foyle.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Eastwood was born in Derry, where he was educated at St John's Primary School (Creggan) and at St Columb's College.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: He later attended the University of Liverpool, where he studied Latin American Studies though he did not finish his degree.

sentences.section: Political career
sentences.text: Eastwood joined the SDLP in 1998 at age 14 to campaign for the Good Friday Agreement.

sentences.section: Political career
sentences.text: He "was drawn to the party by Hume, Seamus Mallon and the other political giants of that time that fundamentally changed politics across the island."

sentences.section: Political career
sentences.text: He was elected to Derry City Council in 2005 aged 22, and elected for a one-year term as Mayor of Derry in June 2010.

sentences.section: Political career
sentences.text: Aged 27, he was the youngest mayor of the city to date.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: Following his election to the Northern Ireland Assembly in May 2011, Eastwood was appointed SDLP representative on the committee of the Office of the First Minister and deputy First Minister.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: He sat on the Northern Ireland Assembly committees on Standards and Privileges, and the Environment and was appointed to the post of Assembly Private Secretary to the Minister of the Environment Alex Attwood in 2010.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: In 2012 he drew criticism from Unionists including Jim Allister after carrying the coffin at the paramilitary funeral of a former Irish National Liberation Army member in Derry.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: A masked Real Irish Republican Army gunman fired a volley of shots over the coffin, although Eastwood stated he was not present at the time of the gunfire.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: He defended his attendance at the funeral saying the deceased was a personal friend and added "I wasn't concerned at the time about who was standing beside me, or about what flag or otherwise was draped over the coffin."

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: It later emerged that party colleague Mark H. Durkan also attended the funeral.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: On 14 November 2015, Eastwood contested the leadership election held at the SDLP's annual conference.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: He beat the incumbent, Alasdair McDonnell, by 172 votes to 133.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
sentences.text: Eastwood was re-elected to the NI Assembly in 2016 and 2017, receiving 5,000 and 7,240 first preference votes, respectively.

sentences.section: Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
Election to the Northern Ireland Assembly
Election to the House of Commons
sentences.text: On 12 December 2019 Eastwood was elected as Member of the Parliament of the United Kingdom for Foyle in a landslide victory against Sinn Féin candidate, then incumbent, Elisha McCallion.

sentences.section: Election to the House of Commons
sentences.text: He was the first of the new MPs elected at the 2019 general election to make his maiden speech in the Commons.

sentences.section: Election to the House of Commons
sentences.text: On 11 November 2020 during a Westminster Hall debate Eastwood called for a full and independent judicial inquiry into the murder of Belfast solicitor Pat Finucane in 1989.

sentences.section: Election to the House of Commons
sentences.text: He was re-elected MP in 2024 following the general election.

sentences.section: Election to the House of Commons
sentences.text: That year, he described the Oath of Allegiance to King Charles III as an "empty formula" and said he took it "under protest" in order to represent his constituents in the House of Commons.

sentences.section: Leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP)
sentences.text: Following the SDLP's poor election results in the 2014 local elections, the 2014 European Parliament election and the 2015 Westminster election, the then SDLP leader and MP for South Belfast Alasdair McDonnell resisted calls to stand down, including from the party's deputy leader Dolores Kelly.

sentences.section: Leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP)
sentences.text: At the SDLP's Annual Conference on 14 November 2015, Eastwood contested the leadership election where he defeated the incumbent, Alasdair McDonnell, by 172 votes to 133.

sentences.section: Leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP)
sentences.text: In July 2021 Eastwood used parliamentary privilege to reveal the identity of Bloody Sunday's 'Soldier F' in the House of Commons.

sentences.section: Leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP)
sentences.text: In August 2024, Eastwood announced his intention to resign as leader, and was succeeded by Claire Hanna at the SDLP Conference on 5 October 2024.

sentences.section: Leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP)
sentences.text: Eastwood revealed in June 2025 that he was considering a candidacy in the 2025 Irish presidential election.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: Eastwood married Rachael Parkes in December 2013.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: They have two daughters.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: The couple separated in 2022.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: In August 2025, Eastwood publicly confirmed his relationship with Labour MP Louise Haigh.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: Haigh was appointed First Secretary of State, Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster and Minister for the Cabinet Office in July 2026.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: Following her appointment, The Irish Times described Haigh as "the most powerful woman in Britain" and identified her relationship with Eastwood as one of her principal Irish connections.

sentences.section: Personal life
sentences.text: The Irish News subsequently noted that, through the relationship, Eastwood was "close to the new prime minister by association".
